candidate_architectures.title: Node.js Range-Extraction Runner with Apps Script Drive Bridge for Persistence
candidate_architectures.description: Node.js on GitHub Actions executes HTTP Range requests directly against Google Drive to read the ZIP Central Directory and extract only selected file ranges, then sends extracted file payloads back to Apps Script via the established eval/POST bridge for Drive persistence.
credential_prerequisites: Requires that the Drive file is publicly readable ('Anyone with the link can view') OR that a Google Drive API Key / OAuth Token / Service Account is provided to the GitHub Actions runner for authenticated Drive download.
strengths: Never downloads the full 993MB archive if only central directory and selected files are read.
Zero risk of Apps Script 50MB blob limit during archive decompression.
Standard ZIP central directory parsing and ZIP64 can be done with minimal I/O (often < 5MB total network transfer).
Reuses existing verified Apps Script createFile bridge for writing output artifacts to Drive.
weaknesses: Direct Google Drive web download links (`drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=...`) often do not honor HTTP Range headers, or return HTTP 200 with the full stream or virus-scan warning HTML for files over 100MB.
Requires authenticated Drive API v3 endpoint (`https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3/files/{id}?alt=media`) to reliably support HTTP Range 206 Partial Content.

candidate_architectures.title: Node.js Streamed Full Download and Selective Extraction
candidate_architectures.description: Node.js downloads or streams the full 993,074,157 bytes from Drive (either directly via Drive API or via a confirmed download mechanism), streams it through a parsing unzip stream (e.g. unzipper / yauzl / node:zlib stream), extracts only configured entries to disk, and pushes them to Drive via Apps Script.
credential_prerequisites: Direct Drive access credentials (or public link handling virus scan confirmation bypass).
strengths: Does not require HTTP Range support from Google Drive endpoints.
Node runner has standard 7GB+ RAM and abundant disk space; 993MB fits comfortably within GitHub Actions ephemeral storage.
Completely bypasses Apps Script blob limits.
weaknesses: Downloads ~947 MiB over the network on every run even if only a 2 KB text file is needed.
Slower execution and higher bandwidth usage.

candidate_architectures.title: Apps Script Drive API UrlFetchApp Range Proxy
candidate_architectures.description: Apps Script uses ScriptApp.getOAuthToken() and UrlFetchApp to query the Drive API v3 endpoint using HTTP Range headers to fetch chunks of the archive, assembling central directory headers or extracted files within Apps Script.
credential_prerequisites: Apps Script OAuth scopes must include https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive or https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly.
strengths: All credentials stay inside the existing Google Workspace domain; no new Google secrets in GitHub Actions.
weaknesses: Apps Script UrlFetchApp payload limit is 50MB and total execution timeout is 6 minutes.
Decompressing raw DEFLATE streams in pure Apps Script JavaScript without native zlib primitives requires custom JS inflate implementations, which are slow and memory-intensive.
High risk of script timeout or script memory exhaustion on large decompressed files.

recommended_architecture.name: Capability-Gated Node.js Selective Range Extraction with Apps Script Persistence Bridge
recommended_architecture.rationale: Separates concerns: GitHub Node.js provides robust buffer processing, zlib decompression, ZIP64 parsing, and HTTP streaming without memory limits; Apps Script provides authenticated Google Drive file creation and metadata verification without having to unpack large blobs. A deterministic capability probe determines whether Drive returns HTTP 206 Partial Content or requires authenticated tokens or whole-stream fallback.

components.capability_probe: A lightweight Node.js probe that sends a 16-byte Range GET ('bytes=0-15') to the target Drive endpoint to verify 206 status and Range header compliance.
components.zip_central_directory_engine: Node.js parser that fetches the tail of the archive (last 65KB to 1MB) to read the End of Central Directory (EOCD) record, Zip64 EOCD Locator / Zip64 EOCD Record if present, and subsequent Central Directory entries without reading archive file payloads.
components.selective_range_extractor: Extracts only target entries: sends Range requests for the specific byte offsets [local_header_offset, local_header_offset + comp_size + header_len], parses the local header, decompresses the payload using node:zlib (createInflateRaw), and computes CRC32.
components.drive_output_bridge: Uploads extracted file buffers to Drive via the established Apps Script eval POST endpoint, invoking DriveApp.createFile with run-scoped naming and destination folder mapping.
components.verifier: Queries the Drive report and independently checks file existence, size, and source archive immutability.

implementation_steps.name: probe_drive_access_and_range_capability
implementation_steps.objective: Deterministically determine whether the source archive is accessible via HTTP Range requests without credentials, with a download confirmation token, or requires a Google Service Account / OAuth token.
operations: Dispatch a GET request for bytes=0-15 using the file download endpoint (e.g., https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3/files/{id}?alt=media or drive.google.com export).
Evaluate response code: 206 (Range supported), 200 (Whole stream returned, Range ignored), 403/401 (Authentication required), or 200 with HTML (Virus scan prompt).
If 401/403 and no token is present, transition to BLOCKED requesting authorized credentials.

implementation_steps.name: parse_zip_central_directory
implementation_steps.objective: Locate and parse the ZIP Central Directory and ZIP64 structures using Range requests at the tail of the archive.
operations: Request the last 65,557 bytes of the archive (minimum needed for standard EOCD comment boundary).
Search backward for EOCD signature (0x06054b50).

Check for Zip64 EOCD Locator signature (0x07064b50) immediately preceding the EOCD record; if present, read Zip64 EOCD Record (0x06064b50) to obtain 64-bit Central Directory size, offset, and total entries.
Perform a Range request covering the entire Central Directory byte range [cd_offset, cd_offset + cd_size].
Parse each Central Directory file header (0x02014b50) into an inventory table: entry name, compression method, compressed size, uncompressed size, CRC-32, and local header relative offset.

implementation_steps.name: match_and_plan_entry_extraction
implementation_steps.objective: Filter the archive inventory against configured target entry names or patterns and generate extraction tasks.
operations: Compare requested entry list from config.actions with central directory inventory.
Verify all target entries exist; report missing entries according to configured on_error policy.
Sort extraction tasks by ascending local_header_offset to optimize network reads and ensure deterministic extraction sequence.

implementation_steps.name: stream_decompress_and_validate_entries
implementation_steps.objective: Selectively fetch compressed byte slices, decompress entries in Node.js, and verify data integrity.
operations: For each target entry, fetch [local_offset, local_offset + 30 + extra_len + comp_size] via Range GET.
Validate Local File Header signature (0x04034b50) and parse variable file name / extra field lengths to pinpoint exact data start.
Decompress compressed slice using node:zlib (createInflateRaw for method 8 / DEFLATE, or pass-through for method 0 / STORE).
Calculate CRC-32 and uncompressed length; assert exact match against central directory metadata.
Stage uncompressed file in run-isolated ephemeral workspace on runner.

implementation_steps.name: persist_extracted_files_via_apps_script
implementation_steps.objective: Transmit extracted file contents to Google Drive through the authenticated Apps Script bridge.
operations: Partition extracted files into chunks compatible with Apps Script POST transport (e.g. base64-encoded in discrete POSTs if file > 10MB, or direct upload).
Invoke Apps Script createFile handler with file name, content, MIME type, and target destination.folder_id.
Capture created Drive file IDs and URLs into execution report.

implementation_steps.name: verify_and_record_run_report
implementation_steps.objective: Produce a comprehensive execution report, persist it to Drive, and assert all verification predicates.
operations: Check source archive metadata (file size and last updated timestamp) to confirm source preservation invariant.
Compile final JSON report detailing probed capabilities, central directory summary, extracted artifacts with Drive IDs, and execution timestamps.
Commit report to Google Drive and verify matching run_id and artifact locators.

verification_predicates.claim: Source archive size and last modified timestamp remain strictly identical before and after extraction.
verification_predicates.evaluation_method: Compare DriveApp metadata recorded in inspect action before extraction with metadata obtained after extraction.

verification_predicates.claim: Extracted uncompressed payload CRC-32 matches the CRC-32 recorded in the Central Directory header.

failure_repairs.failure_scenario: Google Drive download returns HTTP 200 with full stream or HTML virus scan warning instead of HTTP 206 Partial Content.
failure_repairs.root_cause: Drive web front-end (drive.google.com/uc) does not support byte ranges for large unauthenticated downloads.
failure_repairs.repair_action: Switch access_mode to drive_api_authenticated. Use Google Drive API v3 (https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3/files/{id}?alt=media) with an authorized bearer token or Service Account key. If credentials cannot be provided, switch to ARCH_2 (streamed download of the file to disk in GitHub Actions workspace) if confirming the virus-scan token.

failure_repairs.failure_scenario: EOCD signature (0x06054b50) is not found in the initial 65KB tail request.
failure_repairs.root_cause: ZIP archive has a trailing comment or extra data exceeding 65KB, or has ZIP64 spanning records.
failure_repairs.repair_action: Increase tail fetch buffer to 512KB and up to 1MB. Search backward from file length minus 22 bytes.

failure_repairs.failure_scenario: Archive exceeds 4GB or entry count exceeds 65,535 (Zip64 format required).
failure_repairs.root_cause: Standard 32-bit ZIP offsets wrap around at 4GB; 993MB archive may or may not use Zip64, but Google Takeout often employs Zip64 structures.
failure_repairs.repair_action: The parser must inspect the Zip64 EOCD Locator at (eocd_offset - 20). If present, read the 64-bit Central Directory offset and 64-bit entry counts from the Zip64 EOCD record.

failure_repairs.failure_scenario: Apps Script POST payload size limit exceeded when uploading extracted files.
failure_repairs.root_cause: An extracted file is larger than the 10MB-50MB POST body limit of Google Apps Script web apps.
failure_repairs.repair_action: Implement chunked upload or write extracted files to GitHub Actions run artifacts if Drive upload is constrained, or use direct Drive API Resumable Upload session from Node.js runner.
